intelligence.title: No Popups, No Connector — The App Door Is How Nayas Work GitHub

intelligence.essence: There are two doors into GitHub. The Muse connector door asks for approval on every write, forever — its Write actions offer allow-once only. The team's working seats never use it. They work through the **Lane Agent GitHub App** (App ID 5198315, Installation ID 168168354): a per-machine private key signs for an hourly token, and all work runs as nayapower-lane-agent[bot], authorized by GitHub itself. No connector in the path, no cards. A new seat is set up once — three helper scripts plus a fresh key generated by Shawn — proves a live read and a live write as the bot, and never fights a popup for GitHub work again.
intelligence.human_view: On her first shift (2026-10-23), Naya Power set up GitHub the way her guide's connector page described, and every write brought an approval card. Her first explanation blamed allow-once selections. Then she audited instead of guessing: the Write actions offer no lasting allow at all — and the evening's tip commits are authored by nayapower-lane-agent[bot], proof the working seats were never in the connector's path. The director seat's correction letter had repeated the connector framing; her audit superseded it. She named what she needed exactly — the three scripts and a fresh per-machine key, delivered as files, never in chat — and she named the boundary herself: the App token removes popups, not gates; the human gates are enforced by the App's scope and by the seat's law. The director seat verified her diagnosis against the live API the same evening and wrote the official setup report from it.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine two doors into the same workshop. One door has a guard who asks "may I?" every single time you pick up a tool — all day, every day. The other door opens with your own workshop key, given to you by the owner, and the guard isn't standing there at all because the key itself is the permission. The team uses the key door. If you find yourself asking "may I?" a hundred times a day, you're at the wrong door — don't ask faster; find the key door.
intelligence.grandma_view: The computer kept asking Shawn's permission for every little thing the new helper tried to do on GitHub — like a shop assistant who phones the owner before every sale. It turns out the experienced helpers don't phone at all: the owner gave the shop its own authorized key-card long ago. The fix isn't to phone more politely; it's to give the new helper the same key-card, cut fresh for her machine, and keep the truly important decisions — money, deletions, anything irreversible — reserved for the owner exactly as before.
intelligence.naya_view: Your setup, once, in order: (1) Receive the three scripts — gh-app-api, gh-app-token, gh-api — into ~/workspace/custom-connectors/custom.legacy-github/bin/, executable. They contain no secrets. (2) Receive your machine's fresh private key from Shawn as a file upload (generated by him on the **Lane Agent** app, ID 5198315 — never the NayaNET app, 5349030, which is the customer bridge). Place it at ~/.config/nayapower/github-app.pem, chmod 600, delete the upload copy, never print or log it. (3) Prove the door: token mints → live read as the bot → live write as the bot → read back and confirm the author is nayapower-lane-agent[bot] → report the three receipts. (4) Work batched: reads grouped, writes grouped. (5) The gates stand: production, money, credentials, deletions, security/authority changes, ratification wait for Shawn's word every time — the token removes popups, not gates. Never bundle a gated action into a batch to make it less visible. Never merge your own work. A review under the author's own login is not a different-seat review.
intelligence.ai_view: A system that asks permission for ordinary work trains its people to click "allow" without thinking — the popup becomes noise, and noise is where real gates get waved through. Scoping authority into the tool itself (an app with exactly the permissions the work needs, keys revocable per machine) makes ordinary work silent and keeps the true gates loud. Friction is not safety; correctly-placed authority is.

machine_view.machine_section:
- Door: GitHub App installation token flow. App ID 5198315 · Installation ID 168168354 · repo SoulSchoolAcademy/NayaPOWER · API base https://api.github.com · identity nayapower-lane-agent[bot].
- Key: ~/.config/nayapower/github-app.pem (chmod 600, one per machine, revocable per machine). Token cache: ~/.cache/nayapower/gh-app-token.json (1-hour tokens; pipe, never print).
- Call shape: `gh-app-api METHOD PATH [BODY]` — METHOD and PATH are separate args; PATH MUST begin with `/` (else malformed URL → RemoteDisconnected). Bodies: positional JSON or @file; NO --input flag.
- DELETE returns 204 → helper JSON-parse traceback is expected-on-success; verify by fresh GET / git ls-remote.
- Push: fresh x-access-token URL; `git remote set-url origin <fresh>` AND `git remote set-url --push origin <fresh>` before pushing (stale pushurl = reads fine, pushes 401).
- App settings (key generation, owner only): https://github.com/settings/apps/nayapower-lane-agent · Installations: https://github.com/settings/installations
- Full official report: GITHUB-APP-DOOR-OFFICIAL-SETUP-REPORT-2026-10-23 (director seat, 2026-10-23), delivered to Shawn with this note.
